This French Gem Is a Different Kind of Beach Tiny House with a Secret Perk
22 photos
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof
Close enough to the ocean to be a beach house, yet wonderfully hidden among trees and bushes, this unique house on wheels is a wonderland waiting to be discovered.
Apparently plain, yet delightfully mysterious, this French tiny house doesn’t have a fancy name. It’s simply referred to as “The Tiny” (La Tiny), in order to differentiate it from the other houses on the same property, all operating under the new Kof Ha Kof brand, and all equally whimsical.
Located less than ten minutes away (by foot) from the rugged beaches of Kreac’h and Bassinic, in Brittany, but also comfortably close to a hiking trail, The Tiny is a beach house with a twist, perfect for outdoor enthusiasts who want to explore as many adventures as possible. Close enough to the ocean for its guests to feel the breeze in the air, The Tiny was specifically nestled in a romantic grove, for full privacy and no overlooking neighbors.
At the same time, this isn’t a rugged, isolated haven built for an extreme off-grid experience. The abode itself shares the same property as the bigger and smaller hospitality units operated by Kof Ha Kof, and is also less than 2 km (1.2 miles) away from the small town of Plouguerneau, with bars, restaurants, and of course, the famous French bakeries.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof The Tiny is a private sanctuary and a trendy vacation home at the same time. A perfect choice for those who want to be near the beach, it’s also secluded and peaceful enough for intense creative activity of any kind, and writing in particular. In fact, writers were some of the main types of guests that the hosts had in mind when they added this tiny abode to their property.
The house is brand-new. It was delivered this past summer, by La Tiny House, one of the oldest and most reputable tiny house builders in France. They operate a workshop near the famous Mont-Saint-Michel, and their roots go back to more than ten years ago, when the original co-founders built the first two tiny homes in France. Those pioneering dwellings were followed by more than 30 tiny homes completed by 2016.
Since then, La Tiny House has continued to create and build custom homes on wheels with wooden frames, timber claddings, and natural interiors. Artisan craftsmanship took some of the most diverse, quirky shapes, in the hands of this team, and smart layouts were always topped with unusual, but very clever solutions for enhanced functionality.
The custom tiny house built for Kof Ha Kof had to check certain boxes, such as wide openings, a spacious covered terrace, a bespoke bookcase, and a suspended desk. It also had to be an eco-friendly, sustainable abode in two ways, both in terms of the materials used for its construction and furniture, and in terms of how it would integrate into the natural environment.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof Folks at Kof Ha Kof see the beautiful location of their hospitality units as a true paradise on earth that needs to be cherished and protected, not just enjoyed. This also implies encouraging guests to lean toward a more sustainable lifestyle even during their short stay, by using minimal heat for instance (the tiny house was particularly well-insulated precisely for lower energy needs), even though they still have access to Wi-Fi and a TV.
The suspended desk is the unexpected perk that makes this beach tiny house extra-special. More often seen in Australian and Kiwi homes on wheels, this desk concept turns a loft into a multi-purpose space that is more than a bedroom. The main advantage is, of course, space efficiency – when there’s no room downstairs for a classic home office or even a tiny desk, a suspended desk turns the loft into an unconventional office space that still remains a bedroom.
For this particular tiny house, the builder cleverly placed this suspended desk at the outer edge of the loft, not in the back (which is another possible placement, in front of a window). It might seem a bit weird and uncomfortable to let your legs hang in the air while sitting at this quirky desk, but it’s a proven, and popular alternative to classic home offices. Plus, you get the benefit of an expansive view of the entire house, with windows that draw the eye outside.
Especially if you’re a writer, you’d love this tiny, but whimsical space dedicated to your creativity. And there’s more. Downstairs, guests have access to a fully-equipped, rustic-style kitchen, a simple but beautifully-styled bathroom, and a lounge that truly feels like an oasis within an oasis.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof This lounge takes up a big chunk of the floor space, and it’s the first thing you see when you step inside the tiny house. Some might recognize classic features of the popular Nordic style, such as the huge picture window, the natural wood details, and the overall peaceful, dreamy ambiance. However, the builder made this part of the house even better by adding a second, asymmetric window above the oversized one (similar to a classic transom window).
This second window doesn’t just bring in a lot more natural light, but also draws the eye upward and outside – a small, but effective optical illusion that makes a living place seem much more spacious. An elegant L-shaped sofa is the heart and soul of this bright, airy lounge. It offers both comfy seating (with colorful cushions on top of the bespoke upholstery) and generous storage inside its wide, open shelves.
Even the coffee table is a piece of artisan craftsmanship, similar to a vintage treasure chest but also built with open shelves for extra storage space. Colorful artwork, one of the signature features of this French hospitality brand, adorns the lounge and even the kitchen area, adding both a touch of vibrant color and a bit of whimsy.
The built-in bookcase shelves, one of the main requests for this tiny house, sit elegantly above the sofa – big enough to display plenty of books (another signature addition you’ll find in evert Kof Ha Kof abode) but discreet enough to fit with the rest of the furniture, without looking bulky.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof Although compact, the kitchen could very well find its way in any French tiny house intended for full-time accommodation. It has a full-size oven and a small fridge, both tucked under the countertop, a compact induction stove, and a small sink. An open-shelf pantry sitting right between the kitchen and the bathroom provides added storage space for appliances and cleaning supplies.
Instead of bulky upper cupboards, this bright and colorful kitchen has just a couple of dainty shelves and a tiny cupboard mounted on the wall, in addition to the custom-crafted lower cabinets with pigeon hole-style designs.
There’s also a lovely breakfast bar facing the kitchen, cleverly placed under a big window. With two simple chairs, it becomes the perfect dining area for two, complete with whimsical tableware provided by the hosts.
Photo: Lenaig Mevel for Kof Ha Kof Guests also have the wonderful option to dine outside, on the beautiful deck. It’s covered, which means it can be enjoyed any time of the day and in any weather, and it’s a lot bigger than you’d expect: nine square meters (just under 97 square feet).
Envisioned as a beautiful private sanctuary for writers and other creative souls, The Tiny is ultimately a beach house sprinkled with French charm and the revitalizing power of a natural environment.
